title: Stone Soup
text:
Some hungry travelers came to a village, tired and with nothing to eat. They knocked on doors, but every household said it had nothing to spare. Times were hard, and the villagers hid what little food they had.

So the travelers set a large pot on a fire in the middle of the village square, filled it with water, and dropped in a smooth stone. People came out to see what they were doing. Stone soup, the travelers explained. It was delicious, though it would be even better with a little salt. Someone fetched salt. And a few carrots would really bring out the flavor of the stone. A woman went and found some carrots. Perhaps an onion? A neighbor brought onions. One by one other villagers added cabbage, potatoes, a bit of meat, some barley.

At last the soup was ready, and it was thick and rich. The travelers and the whole village sat down together and ate their fill. The villagers marveled that a soup could be made from a stone, and the travelers, in some tellings, left the stone behind as a gift.
lesson: People who will not give to a plea will often add a little to something that is already underway. Start the pot, and invite everyone to contribute one thing.
